desc: Measure the real enrolled-object size ceiling above 256 MiB so the number is known instead of assumed. Ticket 137 probed to 256 MiB and found NO ceiling, and the verifier's --max-object-size default was raised 64 -> 256 MiB as POLICY, not as a measured hardware limit; the maintainer has since assumed 512 MiB, which is not established either. Since ticket 155 deliberately stops trimming, objects will grow and the true limit becomes decision-relevant. TASK: extend the graded-probe method from 137 (zero-filled, 16 KiB-aligned probe objects whose highest loaded offset is reported) to 512 MiB and 1 GiB, and record where iBoot or m1n1 actually stops loading. Remember the two hard constraints that are NOT about size: an enrolled object's TOTAL size must be a whole multiple of 16 KiB, and m1n1's xz decoder advertises 1 GiB. Also time the boots, since single-block xz decompression is single-threaded and decompression latency may become the practical limit well before any size limit. Cheap: probe objects need no distro build. Evidence: done/2026-07-25-t6040-object-size-ceiling.md.
author: claude
result: 2026-07-26 OFFLINE HALF DONE; rig half awaits the maintainer (kmutil is 1TR-only). New scripts/t6040-build-graded-probe.py builds self-describing probes (payload-free m1n1 + 0x5a filler with b'WLOFS'+u64le(offset) at every 0x10C000+k*0x10000). Layout was reverse-engineered from the live-proven probe-graded-256M.bin, and the builder is VALIDATED BY BYTE-EXACT REPRODUCTION of it: rebuilt hash c7fcfa71... equals the value recorded in done/2026-07-25-t6040-object-size-ceiling.md, cmp identical — so it is provably equivalent to whatever produced the probe that actually booted. It self-checks every stamp and asserts 16 KiB alignment before writing. BUILT: probe-graded-512M.bin 59eb0a1a14ded4deb26fb3aeb44041a140c0a76ecbec3be74c5830cb24766cdc (512 MiB = 32768 x 16 KiB, 8176 stamps) and probe-graded-1024M.bin 91e4d692603622dd4bb1fce7f66ef044e0888393dda3639c02266af854725ccb (1024 MiB = 65536 x 16 KiB, 16368 stamps), both on rollback-m1n1-1394c345.bin — the loader currently ENROLLED and the same base the 256 MiB probe used, so size is the only variable. The existing scripts/t6040-probe-load-extent.py already honours PROBE_LIMIT_MIB and needed no change. RIG STEP: enroll a probe, reach Running proxy, run PROBE_LIMIT_MIB=512 ... t6040-probe-load-extent.py; no ceiling looks like HIGHEST LOADED OFFSET one 64 KiB step short of total (the 256 MiB probe gave 0xff0c000), a ceiling looks like LOADED -> zero/stale at a consistent offset. Do 512 first, 1 GiB only if 512 loads fully, then restore the daily-driver object. RECORD CORRECTION: 512 MiB was never established — 256 MiB remains the largest MEASURED size and the verifier's MAX_OBJECT_SIZE. Evidence: done/2026-07-26-t6040-graded-probe-builder.md.
